label: 哲学・思想・批評理論
description: 実存主義からポストコロニアル理論まで、世界の見え方を変える思想書群。

books.title: L'Étranger
books.author: Albert Camus
books.descriptionJa: 母親の死に無関心を装い、やがて太陽のせいで人を殺す——不条理の哲学を小説という形で提示した20世紀文学の金字塔。主人公ムルソーの感情の希薄さが、かえって社会の偽善と生の不条理を浮き彫りにする。たった100ページ強の短さで、読んだ人の世界観を変えてしまう一冊。
books.whyReadJa: 哲学書を読まずして哲学に出会える稀有な小説。漱石や芥川が好きな日本人の感性にも響く、醒めた語り口と実存の問い。
books.selectionReasonJa: 不条理哲学を小説として提示した20世紀文学の金字塔。カミュの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: A man who feigns indifference at his mother's death, and kills a man — because of the sun. A towering work of twentieth-century literature that presents the philosophy of the absurd in the form of a novel. Meursault's thin emotions throw the hypocrisy of society and the absurdity of life into stark relief. Barely over a hundred pages, yet it rewires the worldview of everyone who reads it.
books.whyReadEn: A rare novel that lets you meet philosophy without reading a philosophy book. Its cool narration and existential questions resonate with the sensibility of readers who love Soseki and Akutagawa.

books.title: Le Mythe de Sisyphe
books.author: Albert Camus
books.descriptionJa: 「真に重大な哲学の問題はただ一つ、自殺である」——この衝撃的な一文から始まるカミュの哲学的エッセイ。人生に意味はない。それでも生きる価値はあるのか。岩を押し上げては転がり落ちるシーシュポスの神話に、カミュは意外な答えを見出す。
books.whyReadJa: 実存主義の入口として最適。短く、文学的で、絶望の底から希望を掘り起こす力がある。ニーチェやサルトルに進む前の最初の一冊に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 実存主義の入口として最適なカミュの哲学的エッセイ。
books.descriptionEn: There is but one truly serious philosophical problem, and that is suicide. So begins Camus's philosophical essay, one of the twentieth century's most influential works. If life holds no meaning, is it still worth living? Returning to the ancient myth of Sisyphus, the man condemned by the gods to push a boulder uphill only to watch it roll back down for eternity, Camus finds an unexpected answer: the absurd is not a reason for despair but the very ground of a defiant, self-willed joy in living.
books.whyReadEn: The ideal gateway into existentialism. Short, literary, and capable of digging hope up from the depths of despair. If you are about to move on to Nietzsche or Sartre, this is the essential first book, one you can finish in a single sitting.

books.title: Also sprach Zarathustra
books.titleJa: ツァラトゥストラはこう語った
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.authorJa: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
books.descriptionJa: 山から下りた預言者ツァラトゥストラが民衆に「神は死んだ」と告げ、超人、力への意志、永劫回帰を詩的に説くニーチェ思想の結晶。聖書のパロディとも読める預言書形式で書かれ、近代の価値観を根底から覆した。哲学書でありながら文学としても読める唯一無二の書。
books.whyReadJa: 西洋哲学の最大の転換点。既存の価値観を徹底的に破壊し、自分の頭で考え始めるための起爆剤。ニーチェを読まずして現代思想は語れない。
books.selectionReasonJa: 西洋哲学の最大の転換点。ニーチェの価値転換を詩的に語る。
books.descriptionEn: A prophet comes down from his mountain to proclaim to the people that God is dead, then preaches the Overman, the will to power, and eternal recurrence in soaring poetic prose. Written in the form of a prophetic book that reads almost as a parody of the Bible, it overturned the foundations of modern values and morality at a stroke. A unique work that can be read both as philosophy and as literature, it remains one of the most thrilling and unsettling texts in the Western canon.
books.whyReadEn: The great turning point of Western philosophy. An explosive primer for demolishing inherited values and beginning to think for yourself, it is also the work that gave us the phrase God is dead. No one can discuss modern thought without first reckoning with Nietzsche.

books.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism
books.author: Hannah Arendt
books.descriptionJa: ナチズムとスターリニズム——20世紀を血に染めた二つの全体主義はなぜ生まれたのか。反ユダヤ主義、帝国主義、そして「大衆」の出現を分析し、人間の「複数性」を破壊する権力の構造を暴く。ユダヤ人としてナチスから逃れたアーレントの畢生の大作。
books.whyReadJa: 現代政治哲学の必読書。ポピュリズムや権威主義が再び台頭するいま、全体主義のメカニズムを理解することの切実さは増している。「悪の凡庸さ」の原点もここに。
books.selectionReasonJa: 全体主義のメカニズムを分析した、現代政治哲学の必読書。
books.descriptionEn: Why did the two totalitarian movements that stained the twentieth century with blood, Nazism and Stalinism, come into being? Arendt analyzes anti-Semitism, imperialism, and the rise of the masses to expose a structure of power that crushes human plurality and turns people into interchangeable components of a single machine. Written by a thinker who fled the Nazis as a Jewish refugee, this is the magnum opus of twentieth-century political thought.
books.whyReadEn: Essential reading in modern political philosophy. As populism and authoritarianism surge again, understanding the mechanics of totalitarianism has never felt more urgent. Arendt's later idea of the banality of evil also has its roots here, in this monumental study of power.

books.title: Le Deuxième Sexe
books.author: Simone de Beauvoir
books.authorJa: シモーヌ・ド・ボーヴォワール
books.descriptionJa: 「人は女に生まれない、女になるのだ」——この有名な言葉で始まる、フェミニズム理論の金字塔。生物学・精神分析・歴史・神話・文学を横断しながら、女性が「他者」として構築されてきた過程を徹底的に解剖する。刊行から70年以上、その射程はいまだ色あせない。
books.whyReadJa: フェミニズムの原点にして、いまなお最も深い射程を持つ古典。現代のジェンダー論を理解するための必須の教養。サルトルの伴侶として実存主義の影響も色濃い。
books.selectionReasonJa: フェミニズム理論の金字塔。ボーヴォワールの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman. With this famous opening, the foundational text of feminist theory begins. Ranging across biology, psychoanalysis, history, myth, and literature, Beauvoir dissects the process by which woman has been constructed as the Other throughout the ages, showing how the feminine has been defined against the masculine. More than seventy years after publication, its scope and force have not faded in the slightest.
books.whyReadEn: The origin of feminism and still one of its deepest-reaching classics. It is essential background for understanding contemporary gender theory, and it is deeply marked by existentialism through Beauvoir's lifelong partnership with Sartre. Read it before any other feminist classic.

books.title: Gender Trouble
books.titleJa: ジェンダー・トラブル
books.author: Judith Butler
books.authorJa: ジュディス・バトラー
books.descriptionJa: 「女」というカテゴリーそのものを問い直し、性別は自然なものではなく「遂行的に構築される」と主張した革命的著作。フェミニズムからクィア理論まで、現代の性とアイデンティティをめぐる議論の土台を作った。発表当時は激しい論争を呼んだが、今や現代思想の基本文献。
books.whyReadJa: 現代のジェンダー論の基礎。『第二の性』を読んだ後に挑戦すべき次のステップ。難解だが、読めば「男らしさ」「女らしさ」をめぐる常識が根底から揺らぐ。
books.selectionReasonJa: 現代のジェンダー論の基礎。バトラーが「女」のカテゴリーを解体した。
books.descriptionEn: A revolutionary work that questions the very category of woman, arguing that gender is not a natural given but something performed into existence through repeated acts and discourses. Butler thus laid the groundwork for contemporary debates about sex and identity, from feminism to queer theory. Controversial when it first appeared, it has since become a foundational text of modern thought and is read across disciplines from philosophy to cultural studies.
books.whyReadEn: The foundation of contemporary gender theory and the natural next step after The Second Sex. The prose is difficult, but reading it will shake your assumptions about masculinity and femininity to the roots. A demanding classic that repays every hour you invest.

books.title: Orientalism
books.author: Edward W. Said
books.authorJa: エドワード・サイード
books.descriptionJa: 「東洋」は西洋が作り出した幻想である——このテーゼでポストコロニアル理論の扉を開いた記念碑的著作。文学・学術・政治のなかで「オリエント」がいかに表象され、支配の道具となってきたかを暴く。現代の文化的ステレオタイプの構造を理解するための必読書。
books.whyReadJa: 「西洋 vs 東洋」という二分法そのものを考えるための視点。日本が「東洋」としてどう見られてきたかを知ることで、国際社会での自画像も見えてくる。
books.selectionReasonJa: ポストコロニアル理論の扉を開いた記念碑的著作。
books.descriptionEn: The Orient is a fantasy created by the West. With this bold thesis, Said opened the door of postcolonial theory in a monumental work. He exposes how the Orient has been represented in literature, scholarship, and politics, and how those representations were pressed into service as instruments of domination and empire. A must-read for understanding the structure of modern cultural stereotypes, it remains as provocative today as when it first appeared.
books.whyReadEn: A lens for thinking about the very dichotomy of West versus East. Seeing how Japan has been viewed as part of the East also reveals how it has pictured itself on the international stage. Essential for anyone curious about the politics of representation.

books.title: Peau noire, masques blancs
books.author: Frantz Fanon
books.country: マルティニーク/アルジェリア
books.descriptionJa: 植民地主義が人間の精神に何をもたらすのか——マルティニーク出身の精神科医が、黒人であることの心理的葛藤を鮮烈に描く。言語、欲望、人種差別の内面化を分析し、植民地支配が「支配される側」の魂をいかに破壊するかを告発した。現代の人種論の原点。
books.whyReadJa: 差別が「される側」の精神をどう蝕むかを描いた古典。サイードの『オリエンタリズム』と併読すれば、植民地主義の外と内の両面から理解できる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 植民地主義が精神に何をするかを描く、人種論の原点。
books.descriptionEn: What does colonialism do to the human psyche? A psychiatrist from Martinique renders the psychological conflicts of being Black with startling intensity. Analyzing language, desire, and the internalization of racism, Fanon indicts the ways in which colonial domination destroys the souls of the dominated from within. A foundational work of modern race theory and postcolonial thought, it still speaks directly to questions of identity and selfhood today.
books.whyReadEn: A classic about how discrimination eats away at the minds of those on the receiving end. Read alongside Said's Orientalism to grasp colonialism from both its external and internal dimensions. Indispensable for students of race, identity, and the psychology of oppression.

books.title: Debt: The First 5,000 Years
books.titleJa: 負債論——貨幣と暴力の5000年
books.author: David Graeber
books.authorJa: デヴィッド・グレーバー
books.descriptionJa: 「物々交換から貨幣が生まれた」という経済学の定説は完全な虚構だった——オキュパイ運動の理論的支柱だった人類学者が、負債と貨幣の5000年史を書き換える。古代メソポタミアの帳簿から中世の道徳哲学、現代の金融危機まで、借りと返済の概念が社会をどう形作ってきたかを暴く。
books.whyReadJa: 「お金の常識」がひっくり返る一冊。資本主義のオルタナティブを考えるための必読書で、しかも驚くほど面白い。ハラリの『サピエンス全史』的世界史が好きな人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「お金の常識」を人類学でひっくり返す、資本主義批判の必読書。
books.descriptionEn: The textbook story that money arose from barter is a complete fiction. In this sweeping history, the anthropologist who became a theoretical pillar of the Occupy movement rewrites five thousand years of debt and money, from ancient Mesopotamian ledgers to medieval moral philosophy and the modern financial crisis, showing how the concepts of owing and repaying have shaped entire societies, moralities, and forms of human relationship.
books.whyReadEn: A book that upends the common sense of money. Essential reading for anyone imagining alternatives to capitalism, and astonishingly entertaining to boot. If you loved Harari's Sapiens-style world history, you will devour this in a few sittings.

books.title: On Photography
books.author: Susan Sontag
books.descriptionJa: 「写真を撮ることは、世界を消費することだ」——写真というメディアの暴力性と魅力を、哲学的かつ官能的に論じた批評の傑作。SNSで誰もが写真家になった現代を予見していたかのような洞察の連続。批評家ソンタグの代表作で、読み物としての面白さでも群を抜く。
books.whyReadJa: 批評を読む楽しさを教えてくれる本。写真やSNSに囲まれて生きる現代人にこそ響く。文芸批評・文化批評の入門としても最適。
books.selectionReasonJa: 写真というメディアを哲学的・官能的に論じた批評の傑作。
books.descriptionEn: To photograph is to appropriate the thing photographed. In this masterpiece of criticism, Sontag explores the violence and allure of photography with philosophical and sensual intensity, asking what it means to see the world through a lens. Its insights seem to have foreseen a world in which everyone on social media is a photographer. Sontag's signature work, and unmatched even as pure reading pleasure.
books.whyReadEn: A book that teaches the joy of reading criticism. It resonates most powerfully with modern people surrounded by photos and social media. Also an ideal introduction to literary and cultural criticism, one that makes you look at images differently forever.

books.title: Men Explain Things to Me
books.author: Rebecca Solnit
books.authorJa: レベッカ・ソルニット
books.descriptionJa: あるパーティで、男性がソルニットに彼女自身の書いた本を「解説」し始めた——この笑えないエピソードから「マンスプレイニング」という言葉が生まれた。日常の性差別から暴力まで、フェミニズムの視点をエッセイという親しみやすい形で届ける。軽やかに読めて、深く刺さる。
books.whyReadJa: フェミニズム入門に最適な一冊。難解な理論書ではなく、日常生活の違和感から始まるので誰でも共感できる。ボーヴォワールやバトラーの後に読むと、実践編として腑に落ちる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 日常の性差別を描く、フェミニズム入門の最良の一冊。
books.descriptionEn: At a party, a man began explaining to Solnit the very book she had written, an episode both absurd and painfully familiar that gave birth to the word mansplaining. From everyday sexism to domestic violence, Solnit delivers a feminist perspective in the warm, accessible form of the essay. It goes down lightly, yet cuts deep, and has become one of the most quoted feminist books of its generation.
books.whyReadEn: The ideal introduction to feminism. It begins not with difficult theory but with the dissonance of everyday life, so anyone can relate. Read after Beauvoir or Butler, it clicks into place as the practical companion to their theories.

books.title: Seeing Like a State
books.titleJa: 国家による視覚——なぜ国家計画は失敗するのか
books.author: James C. Scott
books.authorJa: ジェームズ・C・スコット
books.descriptionJa: なぜ国家による大規模な社会計画はほとんど失敗するのか——ソ連の集団農場からタンザニアの強制移住まで、国家が社会を「上から」見て単純化することで起きる悲劇を分析する。グレーバーと並ぶアナーキズム人類学の重要作で、「現場の知恵（メティス）」の重要性を説く。
books.whyReadJa: 政治や行政に携わる人にこそ読んでほしい一冊。「効率化」や「DX」の名の下で繰り返される失敗のパターンが見えてくる。グレーバー『負債論』の次に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 国家計画がなぜ失敗するかを分析する、政治人類学の傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Why do large-scale state social projects so often fail? From Soviet collective farms to forced resettlement in Tanzania, Scott analyzes the tragedies that follow when the state views society from above and simplifies it in the name of order and legibility. A key work of anarchist anthropology alongside Graeber, it champions the value of metis, the stubborn, practical wisdom of local practice that no central planner can reproduce.
books.whyReadEn: A book for anyone involved in politics or administration. It reveals the recurring pattern of failure pursued under the banners of efficiency and digital transformation. The natural next step after Graeber's Debt, and a warning against top-down thinking.

books.title: Imagined Communities
books.author: Benedict Anderson
books.authorJa: ベネディクト・アンダーソン
books.descriptionJa: 「国民（ネーション）」とは、実際には会ったこともない人々が「私たちは同じ国民だ」と想像することで成立する共同体である——このシンプルで革命的な洞察から、ナショナリズムの起源を印刷技術と言語の歴史に求めた政治学の名著。現代のナショナリズム理解の土台。
books.whyReadJa: 「日本とは何か」を考えるための最良のレンズ。サイード『オリエンタリズム』やファノンと合わせて読むと、植民地主義とナショナリズムの複合的理解が得られる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「国民」という概念の起源を解き明かした政治学の名著。
books.descriptionEn: A nation is a community that exists because people who have never met one another imagine themselves as belonging together. From this simple, revolutionary insight, Anderson traces the origins of nationalism through the history of print technology and the standardization of languages, showing how the novel and the newspaper made the nation thinkable. A landmark of political science and the foundation of all modern study of nationalism.
books.whyReadEn: The best lens for thinking about what Japan is and what nationality means. Read together with Said's Orientalism and Fanon's work, it yields a composite understanding of colonialism and nationalism. A short, beautifully argued classic.

books.title: L'existentialisme est un humanisme
books.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
books.authorJa: ジャン＝ポール・サルトル
books.descriptionJa: 「実存は本質に先立つ」——この有名なテーゼを軸に、サルトルが一般向けに行った講演の記録。人間はまず存在し、その後に自分で自分を作り上げていく。自由の重さと責任を引き受けることこそが人間の条件だとする、20世紀で最も影響力のある哲学の入口。
books.whyReadJa: カミュの次に読むべき哲学の入門書。難解な用語を使わずに語られる「自由と責任」の思想は、現代を生きる私たちに直接語りかけてくる。
books.selectionReasonJa: サルトルの実存主義を講演調で語る、哲学入門の定番。
books.descriptionEn: Existence precedes essence. Around this famous thesis, the record of a lecture Sartre delivered to a general audience in 1946. The human being exists first and then makes of itself what it will; to take on the weight of freedom and responsibility is the very condition of humanity. A lucid, accessible gateway to one of the twentieth century's most influential philosophies, it sparked debates that still echo today.
books.whyReadEn: The philosophy primer to read after Camus. Spoken without difficult jargon, this account of freedom and responsibility speaks directly to us living in the modern world. Short enough to finish in one sitting, deep enough to stay with you for years.

books.title: Surveiller et punir
books.titleJa: 監獄の誕生——監視と処罰
books.author: Michel Foucault
books.descriptionJa: 近代以前の公開処刑から、規律・訓練としての監獄システムへ——権力のあり方はどう変わったのか。学校、工場、病院、軍隊に共通する「規律権力」の構造を暴き、現代社会が「監視する社会」であることを喝破したフーコーの主著。パノプティコン（一望監視施設）の概念は現代のデジタル監視社会を予見していた。
books.whyReadJa: 現代思想のマスターピース。SNSの「見られることへの欲望」から企業の人事評価まで、社会の見え方が変わる。サルトルの後に挑戦したいフーコー。
books.selectionReasonJa: フーコーの主著。監視と規律の社会を喝破した現代思想のマスターピース。
books.descriptionEn: From public executions to a carceral system of discipline and training, how did the exercise of power change? Foucault exposes the structure of disciplinary power shared by schools, factories, hospitals, and armies, and argues that modern society has become a disciplinary society through and through. His concept of the Panopticon, a prison designed for constant surveillance, foresaw today's digital surveillance culture with uncanny precision.
books.whyReadEn: A masterpiece of modern thought. It changes how you see everything, from social media's desire to be seen to corporate performance reviews and the layout of our cities. The Foucault to attempt after Sartre, rewarding but demanding.

books.title: Mawsim al-Hijra ilâ al-Shamâl
books.author: Tayeb Salih
books.descriptionJa: イギリス留学からスーダンの村に戻った語り手は、謎めいた男ムスタファ・サイードの秘密を知る——植民地の逆襲、東洋と西洋の欲望の逆転を描くアラブ文学の至宝。「20世紀のアラブ小説で最も重要な作品」と称され、コンラッド『闇の奥』への痛烈なアンサーでもある。
books.whyReadJa: アフリカ文学／アラブ文学の必読書。西洋への「逆植民地化」という視点が衝撃的。アチェベ『崩れゆく絆』と対になる名作。
books.selectionReasonJa: ポストコロニアル文学の至宝。西洋への痛烈なアンサー。
books.titleEn: Season of Migration to the North
books.descriptionEn: Returning to his Sudanese village after years of study in England, a narrator uncovers the secret of the enigmatic Mustafa Sa'eed, a tale of colonial revenge and the reversal of desire between East and West. Hailed as the most important novel in twentieth-century Arabic literature, it is also a searing, deliberate answer to Conrad's Heart of Darkness, told from the other side of the colonial encounter.
books.whyReadEn: Required reading in African and Arabic literature. Its vision of the reverse colonization of the West is startling and unforgettable. Read it alongside Achebe's Things Fall Apart for a matched pair of postcolonial masterpieces.

books.title: The Black Swan
books.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
books.authorJa: ナシーム・ニコラス・タレブ
books.descriptionJa: 「黒い白鳥」——誰も予測できず、起これば世界を激変させる出来事。リーマンショックを予見したかのような（実際には予見していないと自称する）本書は、人間の「わかったつもり」の危険性を哲学・数学・歴史を駆使して暴く。傲慢な専門家を信用しなくなる、危険で痛快な一冊。
books.whyReadJa: 不確実性の時代の思考法。『ファスト&スロー』と対になる「人間の認知の限界」本。タレブの喧嘩腰の文章は好き嫌いが分かれるが、それも含めて読む価値がある。
books.selectionReasonJa: 不確実性と認知の限界を哲学・数学・歴史で暴く、リーマンショック以後に必読となった痛快な一冊。
books.descriptionEn: The black swan is an event no one can predict that changes the world when it strikes. This book, which seemed to foresee the Lehman shock (Taleb insists it did not), uses philosophy, mathematics, and history to expose the dangers of our illusion of understanding the world. A dangerous and exhilarating read, it will stop you trusting arrogant experts, confident forecasts, and your own hindsight.
books.whyReadEn: A way of thinking for an age of uncertainty. It forms a pair with Thinking, Fast and Slow on the limits of human cognition. Taleb's pugnacious, swaggering prose divides readers, but it is worth reading for the argument alone, and even for the style.

books.title: Jenseits von Gut und Böse
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.authorJa: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
books.descriptionJa: 「神は死んだ」の後にニーチェが書いた主著の一つ。既存の道徳観を「系譜学的」に解体し、主人道徳と奴隷道徳という視点から西洋哲学の裏側を暴く。アフォリズム形式で書かれ、後の実存主義やポストモダニズムのすべての源泉になったと言ってよい。
books.whyReadJa: 『ツァラトゥストラ』が詩なら、こちらは理論。ニーチェ思想の中核を論理的に追体験できる。フーコーやデリダに進む前の必須の基礎。
books.selectionReasonJa: ニーチェ思想の中核を論理的に追体験できる主著。
books.descriptionEn: One of Nietzsche's major works, written in the years after the death of God. He deconstructs conventional morality genealogically, exposing the underside of Western philosophy through the lens of master morality and slave morality. Written in pointed aphorisms, it is arguably the wellspring of all later existentialism and postmodernism, and the single best statement of Nietzsche's mature philosophy, a work that still unsettles readers more than a century after it was written.
books.whyReadEn: If Zarathustra is poetry, this is theory. It lets you retrace the core of Nietzsche's thought with logical clarity. Essential groundwork before moving on to Foucault or Derrida, both of whom built directly on the ground this book cleared.

books.title: La Nausée
books.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
books.authorJa: ジャン＝ポール・サルトル
books.descriptionJa: 孤独な歴史家アントワーヌ・ロカンタンは、ある日突然「吐き気」に襲われる。それは世界に意味がなく、偶然に溢れているという実存の啓示だった。実存主義を小説の形で初めて提示したサルトルのデビュー作。哲学書ではなく物語として書かれたことの意味は大きい。
books.whyReadJa: 「実存は本質に先立つ」を感覚で理解したい人に。カミュの『異邦人』と並ぶ、実存主義文学の二大入口。
books.selectionReasonJa: 実存主義を小説の形で初めて提示した、サルトルのデビュー作。
books.descriptionEn: A lonely historian, Antoine Roquentin, is suddenly overtaken by a nausea that rises from the very things around him. It is the revelation of existence: that the world holds no meaning and overflows with mere contingency. Sartre's debut novel and the first presentation of existentialism in fictional form, its famous scene before a chestnut tree root has become a touchstone of twentieth-century literature.
books.whyReadEn: For those who want to grasp what existence precedes essence feels like from the inside. Together with Camus's The Stranger, it is one of the two great gateways into existentialist literature. A short novel with an outsized reputation, fully deserved.

books.title: L'Être et le Néant
books.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
books.authorJa: ジャン＝ポール・サルトル
books.descriptionJa: サルトル実存主義の理論的総体。自由、他者のまなざし、自己欺瞞（マウヴェ・フォワ）といった概念を体系化し、「人間は自由の刑に処せられている」というテーゼに至る。20世紀フランス哲学の最重要テクストの一つ。
books.whyReadJa: 『嘔吐』や『実存主義とは何か』で興味を持ったら、この本格的な理論に挑戦できる。ハイデガー以降の現象学の流れを掴む鍵。
books.selectionReasonJa: サルトル実存主義の理論的総体。20世紀フランス哲学の最重要テクスト。
books.descriptionEn: The theoretical summa of Sartrean existentialism. Systematizing concepts such as freedom, the look of the other, bad faith, and the project of self-making, it arrives at the thesis that man is condemned to be free. One of the most important texts of twentieth-century French philosophy, it remains the clearest and most ambitious statement of what it means to take responsibility for one's own existence.
books.whyReadEn: Once Nausea or Existentialism Is a Humanism has sparked your interest, this is where you can take on the full theory. It is also a key to grasping the current of phenomenology that flows from Heidegger. Demanding, but the payoff is enormous.

books.title: Die protestantische Ethik und der Geist des Kapitalismus
books.titleJa: プロテスタンティズムの倫理と資本主義の精神
books.author: Max Weber
books.authorJa: マックス・ヴェーバー
books.descriptionJa: 資本主義はなぜ西洋でのみ発展したのか——ヴェーバーは宗教改革後の禁欲的プロテスタンティズムが「天職としての労働」という精神を生み、資本主義の原動力になったと論じる。社会学の古典中の古典であり、近代社会論のすべての出発点。
books.whyReadJa: 「資本主義の精神」という言葉の由来を知りたい人に。グレーバー『負債論』と対比すると、近代経済論の見取り図が立体的になる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 資本主義の精神の起源を問う、社会学の古典中の古典。
books.titleEn: The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism
books.descriptionEn: Why did capitalism develop only in the West? Weber argues that ascetic Protestantism after the Reformation produced the ethos of labor as a calling, a disciplined inner-worldly asceticism that became the driving force of the spirit of capitalism. A classic of classics in sociology and the starting point of all modern social theory, it remains the essential reference for debates about religion, work, and the modern economy.
books.whyReadEn: For anyone who wants to know the origin of the phrase the spirit of capitalism. Read against Graeber's Debt, the map of modern economic thought becomes three-dimensional. An indispensable foundation for understanding why we work the way we do.

books.title: Les Damnés de la terre
books.author: Frantz Fanon
books.descriptionJa: 脱植民地化の暴力と、新たな人間の創造。精神病医であり革命家でもあったファノンが、植民地支配が植民者の精神に刻む暴力と、被抑圧者が人間として再生する道を描いた遺著。サルトルが序文を書き、世界中の解放運動に影響を与えた。
books.whyReadJa: 『黒い皮膚・白い仮面』の続編にして、ポストコロニアル思想の実践編。独立運動の現場から書かれた理論の力に圧倒される。
books.selectionReasonJa: 脱植民地化と解放を描く、ポストコロニアル思想の実践編。
books.descriptionEn: The violence of decolonization and the creation of a new humanity. In this posthumous work, Fanon, psychiatrist and revolutionary, traces the violence that colonial rule engraves on the minds of the colonized and the path by which the oppressed are reborn as human beings through struggle. With a preface by Sartre, it influenced liberation movements across Africa, Asia, and Latin America, and remains a founding text of radical thought.
books.whyReadEn: The sequel to Black Skin, White Masks and the practical arm of postcolonial thought. You will be overwhelmed by the force of theory written from inside real liberation movements. A book that changed the course of twentieth-century politics.

books.title: The Human Condition
books.author: Hannah Arendt
books.descriptionJa: 労働、仕事、活動——人間の営みを三つに分け、公共性（ポリスの空間）が失われていく近代を批判したアーレントの主著。「活動」が人間を人間にするという洞察は、現代の消費社会と労働中心主義を考えるための最良のレンズ。
books.whyReadJa: 『全体主義の起源』で歴史を、こちらで人間の根本条件を考える。現代の「仕事に生きる」という感覚を相対化したい人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 労働・仕事・活動を分け、公共性を問うアーレントの主著。
books.descriptionEn: Labor, work, and action. Arendt's major work divides human activity into three, and criticizes a modernity in which the public realm, the space of the polis, is being lost. The insight that action in the presence of others is what makes humans human offers the best lens for thinking about consumer society and the work-centrism of modern life, and for imagining what we lose when politics is reduced to administration.
books.whyReadEn: The Origins of Totalitarianism gives you history; this gives you the fundamental conditions of the human. Perfect for those who want to relativize the modern sense of living for work. A book that rewards rereading at every stage of life.

books.title: Eichmann in Jerusalem
books.titleJa: エルサレムのアイヒマン——悪の凡庸さについての報告
books.author: Hannah Arendt
books.descriptionJa: ナチの大量虐殺の実行役アイヒマンの裁判を傍聴したアーレントが書いたルポルタージュ。「彼は怪物ではなく、考えることを怠った普通の人間だった」という「悪の凡庸さ」論は、世界に激しい論争を巻き起こした。善悪の境界を再考させる不滅の一冊。
books.whyReadJa: 「悪人」を自分と切り離して安心したい人への強烈な警鐘。全体主義が日常に忍び込む仕組みを、裁判記録という具体的な形で読める。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「悪の凡庸さ」を問い、世界に論争を巻き起こしたアーレントの報告。
books.descriptionEn: Arendt's report on the trial of Adolf Eichmann, the operational mastermind of Nazi mass murder, which she attended as a correspondent. Her thesis of the banality of evil, that he was no monster but an ordinary man who simply failed to think, provoked fierce and lasting controversy worldwide. A book about the boundary between good and evil, obedience and conscience, it remains impossible to read without unease.
books.whyReadEn: A violent wake-up call for those who want to comfort themselves by separating evil people from themselves. In trial records you see concretely how totalitarianism slips into everyday life. One of the most discussed and most misread books of the twentieth century.

books.title: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
books.author: Thomas S. Kuhn
books.descriptionJa: 科学は直線的に進歩するのではなく、「パラダイム」の交代によって革命的に跳躍する——このテーゼで科学史の常識を覆した。知識社会学の金字塔であり、「パラダイムシフト」という言葉は今や日常語になった。
books.whyReadJa: 「科学は絶対的な真理の蓄積」という思い込みを解体してくれる。ファスト&スローと合わせて、人間の知の限界を考える入口に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「パラダイムシフト」の概念で科学史を変えた、知識社会学の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Science does not progress in a straight line but leaps revolutionarily through the replacement of paradigms. With this thesis, Kuhn overturned the conventional understanding of the history of science and the image of the scientist as a neutral truth-seeker. A monument of the sociology of knowledge, its phrase paradigm shift has long since entered everyday language, though few who use it have read the book.
books.whyReadEn: It dismantles the assumption that science is an accumulation of absolute truths. Read it with Thinking, Fast and Slow as a gateway to the limits of human knowledge. Short, clear, and genuinely paradigm-shifting in its own right.

books.title: La Société du spectacle
books.author: Guy Debord
books.descriptionJa: 「スペクタクルは資本が蓄積しただけのものだ」——現代社会では、あらゆる経験がイメージの消費に置き換えられている。ドゥボールは状況主義の立場から、メディアと消費社会の全体をアフォリズムで批判する。SNS時代の私たちの状況を60年前に予言していた。
books.whyReadJa: 「映え」や「承認」に追われる感覚が、実は資本の仕組みだと気づかされる。ソシュールやバルトの記号論と合わせて読むとさらに面白い。
books.selectionReasonJa: メディア消費社会を60年前に予言した、状況主義の批判書。
books.descriptionEn: The spectacle is capital accumulated to the point where it becomes image. In modern society, Debord argues, all direct experience is replaced by the consumption of images and representations. From his situationist standpoint, he critiques the whole of media and consumer society in a series of sharp aphorisms. The book predicted our social-media condition sixty years in advance, and it has only grown more accurate with time.
books.whyReadEn: You come to realize that the urge to chase the perfect aesthetic shot and social approval is actually the machinery of capital. Read it with Saussure or Barthes's semiotics for even more. A short book with enormous aftereffects.

books.title: A Theory of Justice
books.author: John Rawls
books.descriptionJa: 「無知のヴェール」の背後で社会のルールを決めるとしたら、あなたはどんな社会を選ぶか——ロールズはこの思考実験から「格差原理」を導き、現代政治哲学の全体を刷新した。リベラリズムの理論的支柱として、いまなお議論の中心にある。
books.whyReadJa: 「格差」について本気で考えるための最良の出発点。分配の正義をめぐる現代の議論は、ほぼすべてこの本への応答である。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「無知のヴェール」で正義を考える、現代政治哲学の支柱。
books.descriptionEn: If you had to decide society's rules from behind a veil of ignorance, not knowing your own position in the resulting order, what society would you choose? From this famous thought experiment Rawls derives the difference principle and renews the whole of modern political philosophy. As the theoretical pillar of contemporary liberalism, it remains at the center of debates over equality, fairness, and the legitimacy of institutions.
books.whyReadEn: The best starting point for seriously thinking about inequality. Almost all modern debate on distributive justice is a response to this book, for or against. Long and demanding, but it is the one work you cannot skip in political philosophy.

books.title: Histoire de la sexualité
books.author: Michel Foucault
books.descriptionJa: 「性は抑圧されてきた」という常識をひっくり返し、近代こそが「語られる性」を増殖させ、セクシュアリティという概念そのものを生産してきたと論じる。「告白」「生命権力」といった概念で、身体と権力の関係を徹底的に問い直す。
books.whyReadJa: 『監獄の誕生』の権力論を身体の領域に応用した続編。ジェンダー・トラブルと併読すれば、身体と権力の現代思想が俯瞰できる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「性は抑圧されてきた」という常識を覆した、フーコーの身体論。
books.descriptionEn: Overturning the common sense that sex was repressed, Foucault argues that modernity instead proliferated discourse about sex, generating endless talk of confession, science, and self-knowledge, and produced the very concept of sexuality. With concepts such as confession and bio-power, he radically re-examines the relation between body, desire, and power, showing how power does not forbid so much as incite and organize.
books.whyReadEn: The sequel that applies the theory of power from Discipline and Punish to the body. Read it with Gender Trouble to survey contemporary thought on body and power from above. A dense book whose ideas are everywhere in modern criticism.

books.title: Les Mots et les Choses
books.titleJa: 言葉と物——人間科学の考古学
books.author: Michel Foucault
books.descriptionJa: 「人間は神話である」——ルネサンス、古典主義、近代という三つの時代で、世界を秩序づける「認識枠（エピステーメー）」がいかに移り変わったかを描き、近代的人間概念の誕生と終焉を告げた問題作。20世紀最大の思想的ベストセラーの一つ。
books.whyReadJa: 「当たり前」だと思っている認識の枠組みが、実は歴史的に作られたものだと気づかされる。現代思想の最高峰の一つ。
books.selectionReasonJa: 認識の枠組みの歴史を描き、近代的人間の終焉を告げた問題作。
books.descriptionEn: Man is a myth. Tracing how the epistemes that order the world shifted across the Renaissance, the classical age, and the modern era, Foucault announces both the birth and the imminent end of the modern concept of man. One of the twentieth century's greatest intellectual bestsellers, the book caused a sensation on publication and continues to be read as a brilliant archaeology of how knowledge is organized.
books.whyReadEn: You come to realize that the frameworks of knowledge you took for granted are historically constructed, not eternal. One of the summits of modern thought, and the source of the famous thesis that man is a recent invention. Challenging, but breathtaking.

books.title: Sein und Zeit
books.author: Martin Heidegger
books.authorJa: マルティン・ハイデガー
books.descriptionJa: 20世紀哲学の金字塔。ハイデガーは人間のあり方（現存在）を「世界内存在」として捉え直し、不安、死への先駆、時間性といった概念から「存在の問い」に挑む。サルトル、メルロ=ポンティ、デリダまで、その後の大陸哲学はすべてこの一冊への応答である。
books.whyReadJa: 難解さで知られるが、実存哲学の最深部に触れる唯一の道。サルトルやフーコーを本気で読みたい人に、挑戦する価値のある一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: 20世紀哲学の金字塔。存在の問いに挑んだハイデガーの主著。
books.descriptionEn: A pinnacle of twentieth-century philosophy. Heidegger reconceives the human way of being as being-in-the-world, and approaches the question of Being through anxiety, being-toward-death, and temporality. From Sartre and Merleau-Ponty to Derrida and beyond, all subsequent continental philosophy is in some sense a response to this one book, which remains as difficult and as generative as when it appeared. Notoriously difficult, yet unavoidable for anyone serious about philosophy.
books.whyReadEn: Notoriously difficult, yet the only road to the deepest recesses of existential philosophy. A challenge worth taking for anyone who wants to seriously read Sartre, Foucault, or Derrida. Go slowly; every paragraph repays the effort.

books.title: Il Principe
books.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
books.authorJa: ニッコロ・マキャヴェッリ
books.descriptionJa: 「目的は手段を正当化する」と要約されることも多い、政治思想史上最も有名で最も誤解されてきた本。君主はどう振る舞えば権力を維持できるか——理想ではなく現実の権力闘争から書かれたこの小冊子は、近代政治学の原点となった。
books.whyReadJa: 理想主義を排して「現実の権力」を考える態度の原型。『正義論』の理想主義と並べて読むと、政治哲学の両極が分かる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「現実の権力」を書いた、近代政治学の原点。
books.descriptionEn: Often summarized as the end justifies the means, the most famous and most misunderstood book in the history of political thought. How should a prince act to win and hold power? Written from the observation of real power struggles rather than from ideals, this small book became the origin of modern political science and the first modern treatise on politics as it is actually practiced rather than as it should be.
books.whyReadEn: The archetype of the attitude that sets aside idealism to think about real power. Read it beside the idealism of A Theory of Justice to see the two poles of political philosophy at once. Short, cynical, and endlessly quotable.

books.title: Zur Genealogie der Moral
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.authorJa: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
books.descriptionJa: 善悪の概念はいったいどこから来たのか——ニーチェが道徳の「価値の起源」を歴史的にたどり、恨みと罪悪感の力学から奴隷道徳の成立を描いた書。現代の批判理論が必ず参照する、道徳哲学を破壊的に組み替えた古典。
books.whyReadJa: 「正しさ」を疑う力を養うための最強の教科書。フーコーの系譜学的方法はここから始まっている。
books.selectionReasonJa: 道徳の起源を歴史的にたどり、批判理論の源泉となったニーチェの書。
books.descriptionEn: Where do the concepts of good and evil actually come from? Nietzsche traces the historical origin of moral values and depicts the formation of slave morality from the mechanics of ressentiment and guilt. A classic that every school of modern critical theory refers back to, it destructively remapped the study of morality, asking not whether moral judgments are true but who benefits from them.
books.whyReadEn: The strongest textbook for cultivating the power to doubt what is taken to be right. Foucault's genealogical method begins here, and almost all critical theory descends from it. Short, vicious, and illuminating.

books.title: Simulacres et simulation
books.titleJa: シミュラークルとシミュレーション
books.author: Jean Baudrillard
books.authorJa: ジャン・ボードリヤール
books.descriptionJa: ディズニーランドは本物の「偽物」であり、現実はすでにコピーのコピーとして拡散している——ボードリヤールはメディア社会の全体を「シミュレーション」の概念で読み解いた。『マトリックス』のネオが読む本として一躍有名になった、ポストモダン論の最重要書。
books.whyReadJa: SNSやバーチャル空間に生きる私たちの現実感覚を考えるための必読書。メディア論・ポストモダン思想の入口。
books.selectionReasonJa: メディア社会を「シミュラークル」で読み解く、ポストモダン論の最重要書。
books.descriptionEn: Disneyland is the genuine fake, and reality already circulates as a copy of a copy. Baudrillard reads the whole of media society through the concept of simulation, arguing that we have lost the difference between the real and its representations. The key text of postmodern theory, it became suddenly famous as the book Neo reads in The Matrix, yet its argument is far more serious and unsettling than the film's use of it.
books.whyReadEn: Required reading for thinking about our sense of reality as people who live in social media and virtual space. A gateway to media theory and postmodern thought. Short enough to read quickly, dense enough to argue with for years.

books.title: Homo Sacer
books.titleJa: ホモ・サケル——主権権力と剥き出しの生
books.author: Giorgio Agamben
books.authorJa: ジョルジョ・アガンベン
books.descriptionJa: 古代ローマで「殺しても構わないが生贄にもできない」とされた人間——ホモ・サケル。アガンベンはこの概念から、主権権力が「剥き出しの生」を生み出す構造を解き明かし、現代の難民・収容所・生命政治を貫く視座を打ち立てた。フーコー以後の政治哲学を代表する書。
books.whyReadJa: 国家の暴力と人間の生命の関係を考える、現代政治哲学の最重要書。難民問題や生命倫理の議論に必須の理論枠を提供する。
books.selectionReasonJa: 主権権力と「剥き出しの生」を問う、現代政治哲学の最重要書。
books.descriptionEn: In ancient Rome, the homo sacer was one who could be killed without penalty but not sacrificed to the gods. From this disturbing figure, Agamben unpacks the structure by which sovereign power produces bare life, a life exposed to violence and stripped of protection. He thereby establishes a standpoint that runs through refugees, camps, and biopolitics today, and that has made him a defining voice in political philosophy after Foucault.
books.whyReadEn: The most important book of contemporary political philosophy on the relation between state violence and human life. It provides essential theoretical tools for debates on refugees, detention, and bioethics. Dark, but necessary reading for our times.

books.title: L'Homme révolté
books.author: Albert Camus
books.descriptionJa: 不条理の世界で「ノー」と言うことの意味。カミュは形而上の反抗から歴史的な革命までを振り返り、絶対的自由（ニヒリズム）と絶対的正義（全体主義）の両方の過ちを批判して、「反抗」の倫理を打ち立てる。カミュ思想の集大成。
books.whyReadJa: 『シーシュポスの神話』の答え編。不条理を受け入れた後にどう生きるのかを考える、実存思想の到達点の一つ。
books.selectionReasonJa: 反抗の倫理を打ち立てた、カミュ思想の集大成。
books.descriptionEn: The meaning of saying no in an absurd world. Surveying everything from metaphysical rebellion to historical revolution, Camus criticizes the excesses of both absolute freedom, which collapses into nihilism, and absolute justice, which hardens into totalitarianism, and sets out a measured ethic of rebellion. The culmination of Camus's thought, it extends the argument of The Myth of Sisyphus from the individual to the political.
books.whyReadEn: The answer to The Myth of Sisyphus. A summit of existential thought on how to live once the absurd is accepted, this is where Camus moves from the individual to society. Read it to see why he remains one of the twentieth century's most read writers.

books.title: Kritik der reinen Vernunft
books.author: Immanuel Kant
books.descriptionJa: 近代哲学の出発点。人間の理性は何を知ることができ、何を知ることができないのか——カントは認識の限界を「先験的」な方法で体系的に問い、哲学のコペルニクス的転回を成し遂げた。以降の西洋哲学はすべてこの一冊への応答である。
books.whyReadJa: 近代哲学の文法を学ぶならここから。ニーチェやフーコーが「乗り越えよう」とした土台が、この書に立っている。
books.selectionReasonJa: 近代哲学の出発点。認識の限界を体系的に問い、哲学のコペルニクス的転回を成し遂げた。
books.descriptionEn: The starting point of modern philosophy. What can human reason know, and what can it not know? Kant systematically interrogates the limits of knowledge by a transcendental method, achieving a Copernican revolution in philosophy by arguing that objects conform to our knowledge rather than the reverse. All subsequent Western philosophy, whether in agreement or in revolt, is a response to this single book.
books.whyReadEn: Learn the grammar of modern philosophy from here. The foundation that Nietzsche and Foucault each tried to overcome stands on this book. Difficult and vast, but the one work that unlocks everything after it.

books.title: Die Welt als Wille und Vorstellung
books.titleJa: 意志と表象としての世界
books.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
books.authorJa: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
books.descriptionJa: 世界は「私の表象」であり、その背後には止むことのない「意志」が流れている。苦悩と欲求を肯定から解放へと導く独自の哲学は、ニーチェ、ヴァーグナー、東洋思想への橋ともなった。西洋哲学と厭世観の出会い。
books.whyReadJa: ニーチェの直接の師であり、実存思想の先駆け。カントの後のドイツ哲学の流れを掴む重要な一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: 意志と表象から世界を解く、ショーペンハウアーの主著。ニーチェの師。
books.titleEn: The World as Will and Representation
books.descriptionEn: The world is my representation, and beneath it flows an unceasing, insatiable will. Schopenhauer's philosophy, leading from affirmation of the will to release from suffering and desire through art, compassion, and renunciation, became a bridge to Nietzsche, Wagner, and Eastern thought. It is the moment in Western philosophy where the tradition meets pessimism, and one of the most readable of the great philosophical systems.
books.whyReadEn: Nietzsche's direct predecessor and a forerunner of existential thought. A vital book for grasping the current of German philosophy after Kant. If you find existentialism appealing, Schopenhauer is where much of its mood was born.

books.title: Enten-Eller
books.author: Søren Kierkegaard
books.authorJa: セーレン・キェルケゴール
books.descriptionJa: 「美的に生きるか、倫理的に生きるか」。キェルケゴールは人間の生き方の二つのステージを、鋭い散文と語りの技巧で描き出す。「実存哲学の父」と呼ばれる彼の出発点となった大著。
books.whyReadJa: 実存主義の起源。カミュやサルトルがその後に問うた「選択」の問題は、ここから始まっている。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「美的か倫理的か」を問う、実存哲学の父キェルケゴールの出発点。
books.descriptionEn: Live aesthetically, or live ethically. Kierkegaard stages the two stages of human existence in sharp prose and dazzling narrative artistry, presenting first the voice of a pleasure-seeking aesthete and then the voice of an ethical judge. The great work that launched the man called the father of existential philosophy, it forces the reader to confront the question of how a life is actually chosen.
books.whyReadEn: The origin of existentialism. The problem of choice that Camus and Sartre would later take up begins here, in this strange and brilliant book. Its alternating voices make it one of the most readable works of nineteenth-century philosophy.

books.title: Frygt og Bæven
books.author: Søren Kierkegaard
books.authorJa: セーレン・キェルケゴール
books.descriptionJa: アブラハムが神の命令でイサクを捧げようとした「跳躍」。合理的な倫理を超える信仰のパラドクスを、キェルケゴールは多層的な語りで描く。「信仰の騎士」という概念で実存哲学の深みを示した代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 「合理的には説明できない選択」を哲学として考えた先駆的著作。実存主義の核心に触れたい人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 信仰のパラドクスを描く、実存哲学の代表作。
books.descriptionEn: Abraham's leap as he prepares to sacrifice Isaac at God's command. Kierkegaard renders in layered narrative the paradox of a faith that transcends rational ethics, a faith that cannot be explained or communicated on the plane of the universal. His masterpiece, which introduces the concept of the knight of faith, plumbs the depths of existential philosophy and remains one of the most moving works in the history of thought.
books.whyReadEn: A pioneering work that treated choices that cannot be rationally explained as philosophy. For those who want to touch the heart of existentialism, this is where the religious dimension of the tradition begins. Short, strange, and unforgettable.

books.title: Pour une morale de l'ambiguïté
books.author: Simone de Beauvoir
books.authorJa: シモーヌ・ド・ボーヴォワール
books.descriptionJa: 人間は「世界の中で自由」でありながら「世界によって制限」される——その曖昧さの中でどう倫理的に生きるか。ボーヴォワールがサルトル哲学を実践の倫理として体系化した、実存主義倫理学の金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: 『第二の性』の土台にある哲学。自由と責任を本気で考えたい人への、実存主義の実践編。
books.selectionReasonJa: 自由と責任の実存倫理を体系化した、ボーヴォワールの主著。
books.descriptionEn: Human beings are free in the world yet limited by the world. How can we live ethically within that ambiguity, neither escaping into bad faith nor despairing of our situation? Beauvoir systematizes Sartre's philosophy into an ethics of practice, arguing that freedom is realized only in relation to the freedom of others. A pinnacle of existentialist ethics and a sustained defense of human responsibility.
books.whyReadEn: The philosophy underlying The Second Sex, and the practical arm of existentialism for anyone who seriously wants to think about freedom and responsibility. More accessible than Sartre's treatises, it is the best place to start with existentialist ethics.

books.title: Kritik der praktischen Vernunft
books.author: Immanuel Kant
books.descriptionJa: 「汝の意志の格率が、いつでも同時に普遍的立法の原理として妥当しうるように行為せよ」。道徳の根拠を理性に求めた、近代倫理学の最重要テクスト。自由と道徳法則の関係を問う。
books.whyReadJa: 「べき」の哲学がここにある。現代の規範倫理学を学ぶ出発点として、カント倫理の全体像を知れる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 道徳の根拠を理性に求めた、近代倫理学の最重要テクスト。
books.descriptionEn: Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law. This is the categorical imperative at the heart of Kant's second critique, the most important text of modern ethics. Grounding morality in reason rather than in happiness, inclination, or divine command, it asks about the relation between freedom and the moral law, and sets the terms for all subsequent debates in ethics.
books.whyReadEn: Here lies the philosophy of ought. As the starting point for studying normative ethics, it gives you the whole picture of Kantian ethics in a more concentrated form than the first Critique. Hard going, but foundational.

books.title: Le Visible et l'invisible
books.titleJa: 見えるものと見えないもの
books.author: Maurice Merleau-Ponty
books.authorJa: モーリス・メルロ＝ポンティ
books.descriptionJa: 身体と世界の関係を根源から問い直した現象学者の遺作。「肉（シャール）」という概念で、主観と客観、見るものと見られるものの二元論を解体する。20世紀フランス哲学の最重要遺産の一つ。
books.whyReadJa: サルトルとは異なる方向の現象学。身体をめぐる現代思想（バトラーも参照）の源泉を辿りたい人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 身体と世界を「肉」で結ぶ、メルロ＝ポンティの遺作。
books.descriptionEn: The posthumous work of the phenomenologist who re-examined the relation between body and world from its foundations. With the concept of flesh, Merleau-Ponty dissolves the dualism of subject and object, seer and seen, arguing that the one who sees is itself visible, caught up in the world it perceives. One of the most important legacies of twentieth-century French philosophy, unfinished but enormously influential.
books.whyReadEn: Phenomenology in a direction different from Sartre. For those tracing the sources of contemporary thought about the body, which Butler also refers to, this is an essential stop. The text is unfinished and hard, but the ideas are luminous.

books.title: Begrebet Angest
books.author: Søren Kierkegaard
books.authorJa: セーレン・キェルケゴール
books.descriptionJa: 不安は罪の可能性として人間に訪れる。キェルケゴールは「不安」を心理学的・哲学的に精緻に分析し、後の実存主義と精神分析の双方に影響を与えた。ハイデガーの『存在と時間』の「不安の分析」もここに負う。
books.whyReadJa: 「不安」を哲学の中心に据えた古典。現代人の不安の構造を理解するための思想的基盤。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「不安」を哲学の中心に据えた、実存主義と精神分析の源流。
books.descriptionEn: Anxiety comes to the human being as the possibility of freedom and therefore of sin. Kierkegaard analyzes anxiety with philosophical and psychological precision, distinguishing it from fear and showing how it discloses the human being to itself. His account influenced both later existentialism and psychoanalysis, and Heidegger's famous analysis of anxiety in Being and Time is directly indebted to this book.
books.whyReadEn: A classic that put anxiety at the center of philosophy rather than at its margins. It is the intellectual foundation for understanding the structure of modern unease, and a bridge to both existentialism and psychoanalysis. Difficult, but short.

books.title: Phénoménologie de la perception
books.author: Maurice Merleau-Ponty
books.authorJa: モーリス・メルロ＝ポンティ
books.descriptionJa: 知覚は心と身体、主体と世界の出会いそのものだ。メルロ＝ポンティは「生きられた身体」の概念から、伝統的な認識論を書き換える。サルトルと並ぶフランス実存主義の基盤を築いた大著。
books.whyReadJa: 身体論の古典。人間を「考える主体」ではなく「生きる身体」として捉える視点が、現代思想の出発点となる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 身体論の古典。知覚と身体をめぐる現象学の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Perception is itself the encounter between mind and body, subject and world. Merleau-Ponty rewrites traditional epistemology from the concept of the lived body, arguing that we do not first have a world and then perceive it, but that perception is the primordial way we are in the world. The great work that, alongside Sartre, laid the foundation of French existentialism and phenomenology.
books.whyReadEn: A classic of the philosophy of the body. The view of the human as a living body rather than a detached thinking subject is a starting point of much modern thought. More readable than many of its reputation suggests, and endlessly suggestive.

books.title: Écrits
books.author: Jacques Lacan
books.descriptionJa: 「無意識は言語のように構造化されている」。フロイトを言語学と構造主義で読み直したラカンの主著。鏡像段階、他者の欲望、象徴界——現代思想と文学理論に決定的な影響を与えた記念碑的テクスト集。
books.whyReadJa: 精神分析と構造主義の交点。フーコーやバルト、デリダを理解するために知っておきたい思想家。
books.selectionReasonJa: 無意識と言語を問う、ラカンの主著。現代思想と文学理論の基盤。
books.descriptionEn: The unconscious is structured like a language. Lacan's major work rereads Freud through linguistics and structuralism, recasting psychoanalysis as a science of the signifier. The mirror stage, the desire of the Other, the symbolic order, the barred subject: this monumental collection of texts decisively shaped modern thought, literary theory, and the humanities at large, and remains one of the most difficult and influential books of the twentieth century.
books.whyReadEn: The intersection of psychoanalysis and structuralism, and a thinker worth knowing to understand Foucault, Barthes, and Derrida. The texts are forbidding, so start with a good commentary. Indispensable for the theory of the subject.

books.title: Mythologies
books.author: Roland Barthes
books.descriptionJa: ステーキのフライドポテト、プロレス、洗剤CM——日常の「当たり前」を記号論で読み解き、ブルジョワ神話の仕組みを暴く。カルチュラル・スタディーズの原点となった、バルトの最も有名なエッセイ集。
books.whyReadJa: 「当たり前」を疑う技術の入門書。広告やSNSを批評的に見る目を養いたい人に最適。
books.selectionReasonJa: 日常の「当たり前」を記号論で読み解き、ブルジョワ神話の仕組みを暴いたカルチュラル・スタディーズの原点。
books.descriptionEn: Steak frites, professional wrestling, detergent commercials, the face of Greta Garbo. Barthes reads the taken-for-granted of everyday life through semiotics, exposing the machinery by which bourgeois values are naturalized and presented as eternal. His most famous essay collection and the origin of cultural studies, it remains the most elegant and enjoyable introduction to the idea that nothing in culture is simply obvious.
books.whyReadEn: An introduction to the art of doubting the obvious. Ideal for those who want to see advertisements and social media critically, and one of the most fun books in the whole theory canon. Read it and you will never look at a detergent ad the same way.

books.title: De la grammatologie
books.titleJa: グラマトロジーについて
books.author: Jacques Derrida
books.descriptionJa: 「脱構築」の思想を提示したデリダの主著。西洋形而上学における文字の抑圧を暴き、「差延」という概念で意味の生成を問い直す。ポスト構造主義の出発点であり、哲学・文学理論・法学まで影響を及ぼした。
books.whyReadJa: 「脱構築」という言葉の出典。近代思想の枠組みを解体するポスト構造主義に触れたい人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「脱構築」を提示したデリダの主著。ポスト構造主義の出発点。
books.descriptionEn: Derrida's major work, the book that presented the thought of deconstruction to the world. Exposing the suppression of writing in Western metaphysics, he re-examines the generation of meaning through the concept of différance, a difference that both defers and differs. The starting point of post-structuralism, it influenced philosophy, literary theory, law, and the humanities generally, and remains the work by which deconstruction is defined.
books.whyReadEn: The source of the word deconstruction, and the best-known gateway into post-structuralism. You will want a good commentary alongside it, but the stakes are clear. Essential for understanding late twentieth-century theory.

books.title: La Condition postmoderne
books.author: Jean-François Lyotard
books.authorJa: ジャン＝フランソワ・リオタール
books.descriptionJa: 「大きな物語の終焉」。科学と知識の正当性は、もはや壮大な物語によって担保されない。ポストモダンという言葉を思想界に定着させた、社会哲学の最重要テクスト。情報化社会の理論的基盤。
books.whyReadJa: 「ポストモダン」という概念の出典。SNS時代の知識と情報を考えるための思想的背景。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「大きな物語の終焉」を宣言した、ポストモダン論の原点。
books.descriptionEn: The end of grand narratives. Lyotard argues that the legitimacy of science and knowledge can no longer be guaranteed by sweeping stories of emancipation, progress, or the march of spirit. The text that fixed the word postmodern in the intellectual world, it is one of the most important works of social philosophy of the late twentieth century and the theoretical basis of discussions of the information society.
books.whyReadEn: The source of the concept of postmodern, whether one approves of it or not. It provides the intellectual background for thinking about knowledge and information in the age of social media. Short, lucid, and endlessly cited.

books.title: The Ticklish Subject
books.author: Slavoj Žižek
books.authorJa: スラヴォイ・ジジェク
books.descriptionJa: 政治的主体は消滅したのか？ ヘーゲルとラカン、マルクスを接続し、ポスト政治的な時代における「主体」の可能性を探る。現代を代表する哲学者の、最も体系的な政治哲学論。
books.whyReadJa: ジジェクの理論の全体像を掴む入門。ヘーゲル弁証法と精神分析を現代政治に使う技法に圧倒される。
books.selectionReasonJa: ヘーゲルとラカン、マルクスを接続する、ジジェクの政治哲学。
books.descriptionEn: Has the political subject disappeared? Connecting Hegel, Lacan, and Marx, Žižek explores the possibility of the subject in a post-political age of consensus and liberal administration. His most systematic work of political philosophy, it brings dialectics and psychoanalysis to bear on the most pressing questions of contemporary politics with characteristic wit and aggression, and is the best single introduction to his thought.
books.whyReadEn: An introduction to the whole of Žižek's theory. You will be awed by the technique of deploying Hegelian dialectics and psychoanalysis on modern politics. His manner can irritate, but the argument repays close attention.

books.title: Ethica
books.author: Baruch Spinoza
books.authorJa: バールーフ・デ・スピノザ
books.descriptionJa: 幾何学の形式で神・人間・幸福を論じる、近代哲学の奇跡。神＝自然（ Deus sive Natura）という一元論と、感情論・自由の思想は、ニーチェやドゥルーズが最も愛した哲学の一つとなった。
books.whyReadJa: 「近代哲学の隠れた王」と呼ばれるスピノザの主著。ニーチェ、ドゥルーズ、そしてスピノザ派哲学の土台。
books.selectionReasonJa: 神＝自然の一元論で自由を問う、スピノザの主著。
books.descriptionEn: A miracle of modern philosophy, arguing about God, humanity, and happiness in strict geometric form, with definitions, axioms, and propositions. Its monism, expressed in the formula Deus sive Natura, God or Nature, together with its theory of the affects and its thought of freedom as self-understanding, became a philosophy treasured above all others by Nietzsche and Deleuze, and by generations of readers since.
books.whyReadEn: The major work of Spinoza, called the hidden king of modern philosophy. It is the foundation for Nietzsche, Deleuze, and Spinozist philosophy generally, and a book that rewards slow rereading. Difficult, but among the most liberating books ever written.

books.title: Die deutsche Ideologie
books.titleJa: ドイツ・イデオロギー
books.author: Karl Marx
books.descriptionJa: 「意識は生活を規定するのではなく、生活が意識を規定する」。唯物史観の宣言書として知られるマルクス=エンゲルスの共同著作。イデオロギーの社会的根源を暴き、後の社会理論の基盤を作った。
books.whyReadJa: マルクス主義の核心的な概念（上部構造・下部構造）の出典。社会を批判的に見る視点の基本。
books.selectionReasonJa: 唯物史観を宣言した、マルクス=エンゲルスの共同著作。
books.descriptionEn: It is not consciousness that determines life, but life that determines consciousness. This joint work of Marx and Engels, known as the manifesto of the materialist conception of history, inverts the relation between ideas and social existence. Exposing the social roots of ideology, it laid the foundation of later social theory and remains the clearest statement of historical materialism and the base-superstructure model.
books.whyReadEn: The source of Marxism's core concepts, base and superstructure, and the clearest statement of historical materialism. It is the basics of a critical view of society, and much shorter in spirit than its reputation suggests. Read it before the Manifesto.

books.title: Manifest der Kommunistischen Partei
books.author: Karl Marx
books.descriptionJa: 「すべての社会の歴史は階級闘争の歴史である」。マルクスとエンゲルスが書いたこの小冊子は、世界史を最も動かした文書の一つとなった。資本主義批判の原点として、いまなお読むべきテクスト。
books.whyReadJa: 世界史を動かした思想の原点。資本主義を批判的に理解するための、最短の入門。
books.selectionReasonJa: 世界史を最も動かした文書。資本主義批判の原点。
books.descriptionEn: The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles. This pamphlet by Marx and Engels, written on the eve of the 1848 revolutions, became one of the documents that most moved world history. As the origin of the critique of capitalism and a model of political rhetoric, it remains a text worth reading today, whether as history, as literature, or as theory.
books.whyReadEn: The origin of the thought that moved world history, and the shortest introduction to understanding capitalism critically. Readable in one sitting, and essential background for almost all political discussion of the last two centuries. Start here, then go deeper.

books.title: Les Deux Sources de la morale et de la religion
books.titleJa: 道徳と宗教の二つの源泉
books.author: Henri Bergson
books.descriptionJa: 「閉じた道徳」と「開いた道徳」——社会を維持する道徳と、人間を超えて開かれる道徳。ベルクソンの最晩年の主著は、生命の躍動（エラン・ヴィタル）の哲学を倫理と宗教の領域へと押し広げた。
books.whyReadJa: 20世紀フランス哲学のもう一つの源流。実存主義と並行する、生命と精神の哲学を体験できる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「閉じた道徳」と「開いた道徳」を問う、ベルクソンの主著。
books.titleEn: The Two Sources of Morality and Religion
books.descriptionEn: Closed morality and open morality: a morality that maintains and defends society, and a morality that opens out beyond the human toward all life. Bergson's last major work carries his philosophy of the élan vital, the vital impetus, into the realms of ethics and religion, and in doing so offers one of the most original philosophies of mysticism and social life in the twentieth century.
books.whyReadEn: Another source of twentieth-century French philosophy, independent of existentialism. You can experience a philosophy of life and spirit running parallel to Sartre and Camus. Bergson's late style is at its most moving here.

books.title: L'Évolution créatrice
books.author: Henri Bergson
books.descriptionJa: 進化は機械的な適応ではなく、生命の創造的な跳躍だ。時間（デュレ）を中心概念に据え、知性と直観を対比させたベルクソンの主著。ノーベル文学賞を受賞した、20世紀初頭の思想的出来事。
books.whyReadJa: 「時間」を哲学した巨匠の代表作。デリダやドゥルーズの前に、フランス思想の基盤を築いた書。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「時間」と「生命の躍動」を哲学した、ベルクソンの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: Evolution is not mechanical adaptation but the creative leap of life. Placing time, la durée, at the center of his philosophy, Bergson contrasts intellect, which spatializes and divides, with intuition, which grasps the flow of life from within. His major work, awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, was one of the great intellectual events of the early twentieth century and reshaped philosophy, literature, and even biology.
books.whyReadEn: The masterpiece of the philosopher who made time his subject. It laid the foundations of French thought before Derrida and Deleuze, and Deleuze's entire philosophy is a meditation on it. A book that reads like a revelation.

books.title: Différence et répétition
books.author: Gilles Deleuze
books.descriptionJa: 「同じものの反復」ではなく「差異の反復」——同一性を前提にしない思想を、ドゥルーズはニーチェとスピノザを接続して構築する。ポスト構造主義の哲学的核心を示した主著。
books.whyReadJa: ポスト構造主義の最重要哲学書。ドゥルーズの世界を理解するための出発点。
books.selectionReasonJa: 同一性を解体し「差異」を考える、ドゥルーズの主著。
books.descriptionEn: Not repetition of the same but repetition of difference. Connecting Nietzsche and Spinoza, Deleuze constructs a philosophy that does not presuppose identity, arguing that difference is primary and that repetition is always the repetition of something singular and generative. The major work that shows the philosophical core of post-structuralism, it is a demanding but exhilarating attempt to think without fixed categories.
books.whyReadEn: The most important philosophical book of post-structuralism, and the starting point for understanding Deleuze's world. Difficult in the extreme, but the concepts are among the most generative of the twentieth century. Read with commentary.

books.title: Mille plateaux
books.author: Gilles Deleuze
books.descriptionJa: フェリックス・ガタリとの共同著作。根茎（リゾーム）、器官なき身体、生成——階層的なツリー構造に代わる、水平で多様な思考の地図を提示する。ポスト構造主義を代表する、自由で野心的なテクスト。
books.whyReadJa: 「中心のない思考」の提案。組織論、芸術、政治にまで応用された、20世紀思想の金字塔。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「リゾーム」の思考を提示した、ドゥルーズ=ガタリの金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Co-authored with Félix Guattari. Rhizome, body without organs, becoming, lines of flight: in place of hierarchical tree structures, the book offers a horizontal, plural map of thought that refuses any center or ground. Representing the most freewheeling and ambitious face of post-structuralism, it has been taken up across organization theory, art, politics, and design, and remains the canonical statement of nomad thought.
books.whyReadEn: A proposal for thought without a center, applied across organization theory, art, and politics. One of the pinnacles of twentieth-century thought, though you will want a guide. Its chapter on the rhizome alone is worth the price.

books.title: The Essential Political
books.author: Carl Schmitt
books.descriptionJa: 「政治的なものの基準は味方と敵の区別にある」。主権とは例外状態を決定する者であるという「友敵理論」は、政治思想史上最も刺激的で議論を呼んだテーゼ。アガンベンやムフが参照する現代政治理論の源泉。
books.whyReadJa: リベラルな政治観の対極にある、現実主義的な政治理論。『ホモ・サケル』のアガンベンが強く影響を受けた書。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「友敵理論」で政治の本質を問う、シュミットの刺激的な主著。
books.descriptionEn: The specific political distinction is that between friend and enemy. Schmitt's friend-enemy theory, and his claim that sovereignty is decided by the one who decides the exception, are among the most provocative and debated theses in the history of political thought. The source that Agamben, Mouffe, and countless others draw on, it remains essential for understanding the darker currents of twentieth and twenty-first century politics.
books.whyReadEn: A realistic political theory at the opposite pole from liberal views of politics, and the book that most strongly influenced Agamben of Homo Sacer. Disturbing and clear-sighted in equal measure. Essential for anyone who wants to take politics seriously.

books.title: The Social Construction of Reality
books.author: Peter L. Berger
books.descriptionJa: 現実は客観的に存在するのではなく、人間の日常的相互作用によって「社会的に構成」される。現象学的社会学の古典。社会が個人を作り、個人が社会を作る循環を、日常世界の分析から明らかにする。
books.whyReadJa: 「当たり前の世界は作られたもの」という視点の古典的根拠。社会学と知識論の架け橋。
books.selectionReasonJa: 現実は社会的に構成されることを示した、現象学的社会学の古典。
books.descriptionEn: Reality does not exist objectively but is socially constructed through human everyday interaction. This classic of phenomenological sociology, written with Thomas Luckmann, shows how the world appears to us as objective fact while being continuously produced and maintained by individuals in conversation. From the analysis of the lifeworld, it reveals the cycle in which society makes the individual and the individual makes society.
books.whyReadEn: The classical basis of the view that the taken-for-granted world is constructed. It forms a bridge between sociology and the theory of knowledge, and is the ancestor of much contemporary thought about institutions. Short, clear, and quietly revolutionary.

books.title: Essai sur le don
books.author: Marcel Mauss
books.descriptionJa: 「贈与には必ず返礼が伴う」。原始社会の交換システムを分析し、贈与・受領・返礼の三つの義務が社会を結びつけることを示す。現代社会学・人類学・哲学（デリダの『贈与の時間』）の原点となった古典。
books.whyReadJa: グレーバー『負債論』や経済人類学の理論的源泉。資本主義を相対化するための最重要人類学書。
books.selectionReasonJa: 贈与が社会を結ぶことを示した、人類学の古典。
books.descriptionEn: Every gift entails a return. Analyzing exchange systems in archaic societies, Mauss shows that the three obligations, to give, to receive, and to repay, bind society together and create relations of prestige, alliance, and honor. A classic that stands at the origin of modern sociology, anthropology, and philosophy, it is the book behind a vast literature, from structuralism to Derrida's Given Time and Graeber's Debt.
books.whyReadEn: The theoretical source of Graeber's Debt and of economic anthropology, and the most important anthropological work for relativizing capitalism. Short and elegant, it is one of the rare books that launched an entire field. Read it before or after Graeber.

books.title: De la division du travail social
books.author: Émile Durkheim
books.authorJa: エミール・デュルケーム
books.descriptionJa: 近代社会はなぜ「個」を重視するのか。デュルケームは社会の連帯を「機械的連帯」と「有機的連帯」に分け、分業が道徳秩序を作ることを論じる。社会学という学問の成立を告げた古典。
books.whyReadJa: 社会学の創設者の主著。社会と個人の関係を考えるための、理論的出発点。
books.selectionReasonJa: 社会の連帯を問う、社会学の創設者デュルケームの主著。
books.titleEn: The Division of Labour in Society
books.descriptionEn: Why does modern society value the individual, when traditional society submerges the person in the group? Durkheim distinguishes mechanical solidarity, based on likeness, from organic solidarity, based on interdependence and the division of labor, and argues that the division of labor creates moral order rather than destroying it. The classic that announced the founding of sociology as a discipline, it remains a touchstone for thinking about modern social cohesion.
books.whyReadEn: The major work of the founder of sociology, and a theoretical starting point for thinking about the relation between society and the individual. Clearer and more readable than its reputation suggests. Essential background for understanding how modern individualism arose.

books.title: Le Suicide
books.author: Émile Durkheim
books.authorJa: エミール・デュルケーム
books.descriptionJa: 自殺は個人の心理の問題ではなく、社会の状態を映す鏡である。デュルケームは統計データから自殺の社会的類型を析出し、「社会的事実」を実証する方法を確立した。社会学の方法論的転換点。
books.whyReadJa: 「個人の問題」を社会学的に読み直す古典。データと理論を組み合わせる学問の手本。
books.selectionReasonJa: 自殺を社会の鏡として読み解く、社会学の方法論的転換点。
books.descriptionEn: Suicide is not a problem of individual psychology but a mirror reflecting the state of society. From statistical data, Durkheim derives social types of suicide, egoistic, altruistic, and anomic, and shows that the suicide rate varies systematically with the degree of social integration. A methodological turning point in sociology, it established the rule that social facts must be explained by social causes.
books.whyReadEn: A classic that rereads personal problems sociologically, showing that the most individual act is patterned by society. A model of combining data and theory, and the founding demonstration that social facts exist. Essential for anyone interested in social science method.

books.title: Les Formes élémentaires de la vie religieuse
books.author: Émile Durkheim
books.authorJa: エミール・デュルケーム
books.descriptionJa: 宗教は社会が自分自身を祀る儀式である。オーストラリアのトーテム宗教を分析し、集合的沸騰と聖と俗の区別から宗教の起源を論じる。宗教社会学と象徴論の古典。
books.whyReadJa: 「神話・宗教の社会的起源」を考える基本文献。アンダーソン『想像の共同体』も参照する重要な書。
books.selectionReasonJa: 宗教の社会的起源を論じた、宗教社会学の古典。
books.titleEn: The Elementary Forms of Religious Life
books.descriptionEn: Religion is a ritual in which society worships itself. Analyzing the totemic religion of Australian aborigines, Durkheim derives the origin of religious belief from collective effervescence and the distinction between the sacred and the profane, arguing that the gods are society transfigured. A classic of the sociology of religion and of symbolism, it influenced everything from structuralism to the study of collective behavior and is cited directly in Anderson's Imagined Communities.
books.whyReadEn: Foundational literature for thinking about the social origins of myth and religion, and a book cited directly by Anderson in Imagined Communities. Long, but the central argument repays the effort. Essential for the theory of the sacred and of collective life.

books.title: Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft
books.author: Max Weber
books.authorJa: マックス・ヴェーバー
books.descriptionJa: 官僚制、支配の諸類型、資本主義の精神——ヴェーバーの社会学を体系化した大著。近代化とは「合理化」の過程であるという分析は、現代社会論の最重要の枠組みとなった。
books.whyReadJa: 近代社会の「型」を体系化した書。組織論・政治学・社会学の基本的な概念の出典。
books.selectionReasonJa: 官僚制と支配の類型で近代を体系化した、ヴェーバー社会学の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Bureaucracy, the types of domination, the forms of legitimate authority, the spirit of capitalism: this is the great work that systematizes Weber's sociology. Its analysis of modernization as a process of rationalization, and its typology of legal-rational, traditional, and charismatic domination, became the most important framework of modern social theory, and the book remains the reference point for the study of organizations, the state, and modern life.
books.whyReadEn: A book that systematized the types of modern society, and the source of basic concepts used across organization theory, political science, and sociology. Dense and encyclopedic, so read selectively. Indispensable for understanding rationalization and bureaucracy.

books.title: L'Archéologie du savoir
books.author: Michel Foucault
books.descriptionJa: 「言説」の分析を方法論として確立する、フーコーの理論的主著。知は断絶とともに形成され、権力と結びつく。『言葉と物』の方法的基礎を明らかにし、言説分析の出発点となった。
books.whyReadJa: フーコーの方法論の中核。『監獄の誕生』『性の歴史』の理論的土台を理解したい人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 言説分析の方法論を確立した、フーコーの理論的主著。
books.descriptionEn: Foucault's theoretical major work, establishing the analysis of discourse as a method. Knowledge is formed through ruptures and discontinuities rather than continuous progress, and discourses are bound up with institutional power. It clarifies the methodological basis of The Order of Things and became the starting point of discourse analysis across the humanities and social sciences, from literary studies to the history of science.
books.whyReadEn: The core of Foucault's method, and essential for understanding the theoretical ground of Discipline and Punish and The History of Sexuality. More abstract than those works, but it shows the machinery. Read it after the case studies, not before.

books.title: Naissance de la clinique
books.author: Michel Foucault
books.descriptionJa: 近代医学は「まなざし」を獲得した。病院という空間と医学の言語が、人間の身体をどう構成してきたかを歴史的に分析する。フーコーの初期三部作をなす、権力と知の考古学。
books.whyReadJa: 「医療は科学以前に権力構造である」という視点。身体と制度をめぐるフーコー思想の出発点。
books.selectionReasonJa: 医療と権力の関係を問う、フーコー初期の考古学。
books.descriptionEn: Modern medicine acquired the gaze. Foucault historically analyzes how the space of the hospital and the language of clinical medicine constituted the human body as an object of knowledge, and how the clinic organized a new way of seeing illness and death. An archaeology of power and knowledge that forms the early trilogy of Foucault's work together with Madness and Civilization and The Order of Things.
books.whyReadEn: The view that medicine is a structure of power before it is a science. It is the starting point of Foucault's thought on the body and institutions, and the clearest early example of his method. Read it with Discipline and Punish.

books.title: Folie et déraison
books.author: Michel Foucault
books.descriptionJa: 狂気は「自然の病」ではなく、近代が作り出した排除のカテゴリーである。精神病院の誕生とともに、理性と非理性の境界がどう引かれたかを歴史的に追う。フーコーを一躍有名にした問題作。
books.whyReadJa: 「排除」を制度の歴史として描いた古典。精神病・障害・マイノリティを考えるための思想的地平。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「狂気」を排除の制度として描いた、フーコーの問題作。
books.descriptionEn: Madness is not a natural disease but a category of exclusion created by modernity. Foucault traces historically how the boundary between reason and unreason was drawn and redrawn, from the ship of fools to the birth of the asylum and the medicalization of the mad. The problematizing work that made Foucault famous, it remains a foundational text for thinking about psychiatry, disability, exclusion, and the politics of normality.
books.whyReadEn: A classic that recounts exclusion as a history of institutions, and an intellectual horizon for thinking about mental illness, disability, and minorities. Sometimes criticized for its historical accuracy, but indispensable as a provocation. The essential entry point to Foucault.

books.title: Saussure's Course in General Linguistics
books.author: Ferdinand de Saussure
books.authorJa: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
books.descriptionJa: 「言語は差異の体系である」。シニフィアンとシニフィエ、ラングとパロール——構造主義の理論的基盤を築いたソシュールの講義録。現代思想のあらゆる領域が参照する、20世紀思想の最重要テクストの一つ。
books.whyReadJa: 構造主義の原点。記号の仕組みを知れば、バルト、ラカン、デリダが一気に理解しやすくなる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 構造主義の理論的基盤。言語は差異の体系である、ソシュールの講義録。
books.descriptionEn: Language is a system of differences. In these reconstructed lectures, Saussure laid out the principles that became the theoretical basis of structuralism: the arbitrary sign, the distinction between signifier and signified, and the distinction between langue, the system, and parole, individual speech. One of the most important texts of twentieth-century thought, it is referenced by every domain of the modern humanities and made linguistics a model science.
books.whyReadEn: The origin of structuralism. Understand how signs work and Barthes, Lacan, and Derrida become far easier to grasp, since all of them build on Saussure. Short and surprisingly readable for such a foundational text. Essential.

books.title: Wahrheit und Methode
books.author: Hans-Georg Gadamer
books.authorJa: ハンス＝ゲオルク・ガーダマー
books.descriptionJa: 解釈学の復権。理解とは方法の適用ではなく、伝統と現在が融合する「地平の融合」である。自然科学の客観主義に対し、人文科学の真理を擁護した20世紀ドイツ哲学の古典。
books.whyReadJa: 「理解すること」の本質を哲学した書。テクスト解釈の理論を知りたい人に必読。
books.selectionReasonJa: 解釈学の復権。理解を「地平の融合」として問う、ガーダマーの古典。
books.descriptionEn: The rehabilitation of hermeneutics. Gadamer argues that understanding is not the application of method but the fusion of horizons, in which the tradition of the past and the present situation of the interpreter come together. Against the objectivism of the natural sciences, he defends the truth of the human sciences, and his analysis of prejudice, tradition, and effective history transformed philosophy, theology, law, and literary theory.
books.whyReadEn: A book that philosophized the essence of understanding, and required reading for anyone who wants the theory of textual interpretation. The idea of the fusion of horizons is one of the most useful concepts in the humanities. Dense but rewarding.

books.title: Om Begrebet Ironi
books.author: Søren Kierkegaard
books.authorJa: セーレン・キェルケゴール
books.descriptionJa: イロニーは単なる修辞ではなく、有限なものへの無限な否定である。ソクラテスの実践を分析し、イロニーを実存の哲学的態度として確立した、キェルケゴールの学位論文。
books.whyReadJa: 「イロニー」という概念の哲学的源泉。文学批評や現代思想が使う用語の背景を理解する。
books.selectionReasonJa: イロニーを実存の哲学的態度として確立した、キェルケゴールの学位論文。
books.descriptionEn: Irony is not mere rhetoric but infinite absolute negativity toward finitude. In his doctoral thesis, Kierkegaard analyzes Socratic practice and establishes irony as a philosophical attitude of existence, a standpoint from which the given world is held at a distance. The book is a brilliant prelude to his later works, and the philosophical source of a concept that pervades literary criticism and modern thought.
books.whyReadEn: The philosophical source of the concept of irony, and essential for understanding a term used throughout literary criticism and modern thought. Read it to see how Kierkegaard used irony to hold the whole world at a distance. A demanding but eye-opening doctorate.

books.title: La Production de l'espace
books.author: Henri Lefebvre
books.authorJa: アンリ・ルフェーヴル
books.descriptionJa: 空間は容器ではなく、社会的に生産される。都市、資本、日常生活を貫く空間論を提示し、現代の都市研究・地理学・カルチュラル・スタディーズの基盤を築いた。20世紀フランス社会思想の金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: 「空間」を社会理論の中核に据えた書。都市論やデザイン、建築に興味がある人に必読。
books.selectionReasonJa: 空間は社会的に生産されることを示した、ルフェーヴルの金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Space is not a container but something socially produced. Presenting a theory of space that runs through the city, capital, everyday life, and the state, Lefebvre laid the foundations of urban studies, geography, and cultural studies. His triad of spatial practice, representations of space, and representational spaces has been enormously influential, and the book remains a key reference for anyone interested in how power and capital shape the spaces we inhabit.
books.whyReadEn: A book that placed space at the center of social theory, and required reading for anyone interested in urban theory, design, or architecture. Its ideas have shaped entire disciplines. Long, but the opening sections are worth the time alone.

books.title: 論語
books.author: Confucius
books.descriptionJa: 「学んで時にこれを習う、亦た説ばしからずや」。孔子と弟子たちの対話をまとめた、東アジア2000年の思想の源泉。仁・義・礼・智の徳を、簡潔な言葉で語る。
books.whyReadJa: 東アジアの思考の基盤。西洋哲学と並ぶ、もう一つの知の系譜に触れるための最重要書。
books.selectionReasonJa: 東アジア思想の源流。西洋哲学と対になる、もう一つの哲学的伝統の古典。
books.descriptionEn: Is it not a joy to practice what you learn at due times? The dialogues of Confucius and his disciples, collected after his death, are the wellspring of two thousand years of East Asian thought. In plain and often enigmatic words, the Analects sets out the virtues of ren, humanity, yi, righteousness, li, propriety, and zhi, wisdom, and the way a person should live in relation to others, family, and the state.
books.whyReadEn: The foundation of East Asian thinking, and the most important book for touching a lineage of knowledge that runs parallel to Western philosophy. Short, aphoristic, and endlessly quotable. Read it slowly, one passage at a time.

books.title: 孫子
books.author: Sun Tzu
books.descriptionJa: 「彼を知り己を知らば、百戦して殆からず」。2500年前の兵法書が、戦争を超えて現代のビジネスや政治に読まれ続ける理由。戦略的思考の古典。
books.whyReadJa: 「戦略」を考える基本書。西洋の哲学書とは異なる、東アジアの実践的知恵の源泉。
books.selectionReasonJa: 東アジア戦略思想の古典。ビジネス・政治にも応用される、最も読まれる東洋の書。
books.descriptionEn: Know the enemy and know yourself, and in a hundred battles you will never be in peril. A military treatise from 2,500 years ago, The Art of War continues to be read far beyond the battlefield, in modern business, politics, and even sports. Its reflections on strategy, deception, terrain, and the economy of force remain the most concise and influential statement of strategic thinking in the East Asian tradition.
books.whyReadEn: The basic text for thinking about strategy, and a source of East Asian practical wisdom quite different from Western philosophical books. Short, quotable, and endlessly applied in business and politics. Read it with Machiavelli for a matched pair on power.

books.title: 善の研究
books.author: Nishida Kitaro
books.descriptionJa: 「純粋経験」から出発し、善と美、宗教を一元論的に論じる。西洋哲学を土台にしながら、東洋の体験を哲学として結晶させた、日本哲学の出発点。
books.whyReadJa: 日本発の哲学。西洋思想を輸入するだけでなく、日本から哲学を生み出した記念碑。
books.selectionReasonJa: 日本哲学の出発点。西洋哲学と東洋思想を統合した、アジア思想の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Starting from pure experience, Nishida argues monistically about good, beauty, and religion, developing a philosophy that builds on Western thought while crystallizing Eastern experience, particularly Zen, into systematic philosophy. An Inquiry into the Good is the founding work of the Kyoto School and of Japanese philosophy as a whole, and it remains the clearest and most moving statement of a philosophy born in Japan rather than imported.
books.whyReadEn: Philosophy born in Japan: a landmark that did not merely import Western thought but produced a new philosophy from Japanese experience itself. The founding text of the Kyoto School. Challenging, but the starting point of an entire national tradition.

books.title: Πολιτεία
books.author: Plato
books.descriptionJa: 西洋哲学の原点にして、あらゆる政治思想が参照し続ける対話篇。正義とは何か、理想国家とは何かをソクラテスの対話を通して追究する。哲人王の統治、教育、詩の検閲まで、法や統治、教育にいたるまで、現代でも議論される問いのほとんどがここに登場する。
books.whyReadJa: 西洋哲学のすべての出発点。正義や理想社会について、先入観なしにゼロから考えるための最良の入り口。
books.selectionReasonJa: 西洋哲学・政治思想の原点として、正義・国家・教育をめぐる世界の見方の基礎を築いた最重要古典。
books.descriptionEn: The origin of Western philosophy and a dialogue that every subsequent political theory keeps returning to. Through Socrates' conversations, Plato pursues the question of what justice is and what an ideal state would look like. From the rule of philosopher-kings and the education of citizens to the censorship of poetry, nearly every question still debated today about law, governance, and education makes its first appearance here, and in its most memorable form.
books.whyReadEn: The starting point of all Western philosophy. The best entry into thinking about justice and the ideal society from scratch, with no preconceptions—the clearest map of the territory all later thought walks through.

books.title: Ἠθικὰ Νικομάχεια
books.author: Aristotle
books.descriptionJa: 「幸福（エウダイモニア）」とは何か。アリストテレスが人間の善き生の全体を体系的に考察した倫理学の始祖にして最高峰。徳、友愛、快楽、実践知——「人はいかに生きるべきか」という問いへの、二千四百年を経ても色褪せない古典的回答がここにある。
books.whyReadJa: 「よい人生とは何か」を最澄な形で論じた書。幸福論の古典として、人生の羅針盤を手に入れるための入門書。
books.selectionReasonJa: 西洋倫理学の始祖にして最高傑作。善き生と幸福をめぐる問いの、すべての出発点として選んだ。
books.descriptionEn: What is eudaimonia—the good life, human flourishing? In this foundational and still unsurpassed work of ethics, Aristotle systematically examines the whole of a human being's good life. Virtue, friendship, pleasure, practical wisdom: his classical answer to the question 'How should one live?' has lost none of its power in twenty-four hundred years. It offers not abstract rules but a practical ethics for living, and its account of happiness as activity in accordance with virtue remains the most influential in Western thought.
books.whyReadEn: The most rigorous treatise on what makes a good life. A classic of eudaimonia and practical wisdom, it is the essential introduction to getting your bearings in the art of living.

books.title: Leviathan
books.author: Thomas Hobbes
books.descriptionJa: 「万人の万人に対する戦い」——自然状態にある人間は互いに敵であり、平和を求めて国家（リヴァイアサン）に権力を譲渡する。王権神授説を否定し、国家を人間の制作物として初めて体系的に論じた近代政治学の金字塔。主権、法、自由をめぐる議論の出発点。
books.whyReadJa: 「国家とは何か」をゼロから組み立てた近代政治学の祖。権力と自由を考えるすべての議論はここに遡る。
books.selectionReasonJa: 近代政治思想の起点。国家と主権を人間の制作物として論じた、政治学を生んだ最重要古典。
books.descriptionEn: 'The war of all against all'—in the state of nature, human beings are mutual enemies, and out of the desire for peace they transfer their power to a state, the Leviathan. Denying the divine right of kings, Hobbes was the first to systematically treat the state as a human artifact. This cornerstone of modern political science is the starting point of every argument about sovereignty, law, and liberty. Its portrait of human fear, reason, and the price of security remains uncomfortably alive today.
books.whyReadEn: The founding father of modern political thought, building the state from scratch. Every argument about power, freedom, and order—from democracy to dictatorship—traces back to this book. It is the essential map of how authority is born.

books.title: Du contrat social
books.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
books.authorJa: ジャン＝ジャック・ルソー
books.descriptionJa: 「人間は生まれながらにして自由であるが、至る所で鎖につながれている」——この有名な書き出しで始まる、自由と社会をめぐる近代思想の絶対的な古典。人民主権と一般意志の思想を打ち立て、フランス革命から民主主義の現実まで、あらゆる革命思想の源泉となった。
books.whyReadJa: 民主主義の原典。一般意志と人民主権の思想は、現代の自由と統治を考えるうえで欠かせない。
books.selectionReasonJa: 近代民主主義の理念を確立した古典。フランス革命に思想的火を点けた、革命思想の源泉。
books.descriptionEn: 'Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.' This famous opening line begins the absolute classic of modern thought on freedom and society. Rousseau established the ideas of popular sovereignty and the general will, becoming the wellspring of revolutionary thought from the French Revolution to the realities of democracy today. No other book has inspired so many revolutions with so few pages. It remains the clearest statement of the puzzle: how can we be both free and governed?
books.whyReadEn: The original text of democracy. The ideas of the general will and popular sovereignty are indispensable to thinking about freedom, government, and the legitimacy of power today. A short book, yet the seed of the modern democratic age.

books.title: Phänomenologie des Geistes
books.author: G.W.F. Hegel
books.descriptionJa: 意識が自己の学びによって精神の高みへと上昇していく過程を描く、ヘーゲル哲学の最大の難所にして最高峰。主人と奴隷の弁証法をはじめ、理性、絶対知にいたるまで、実存主義からマルクス、フランクフルト学派にいたる近代思想全体の源泉となった大著。
books.whyReadJa: 近代思想全体の源流。弁証法の思考を体得すれば、哲学史を一望できるようになる難関にして名峰。
books.selectionReasonJa: ヘーゲル哲学の最高峰。弁証法を生み、マルクスから実存主義まで近代思想全体に影響を与えた。
books.descriptionEn: A monumental and formidable ascent: the chronicle of consciousness educating itself toward the height of Spirit. From the famous dialectic of master and slave to reason and absolute knowing, this is the source of virtually all modern thought—from Marxism to existentialism and the Frankfurt School. Hegel's greatest work, and the summit of his philosophy, it is at once the most difficult and the most generative book in all of modern philosophy.
books.whyReadEn: The source of modern thought itself. Master the dialectic and the whole history of philosophy comes into view—a difficult mountain, but the grandest and the most rewarding one to climb.

books.title: Logisch-philosophische Abhandlung
books.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
books.authorJa: ルートヴィヒ・ウィトゲンシュタイン
books.descriptionJa: 「語りうることは明晰に語りうる。語りえないことについては、沈黙しなければならない」——世界は事実の総体であり、言語は世界を写し取る絵である。わずか数十ページに番号づけられた命題を詰め込み、論理学、言語哲学、そして世界観までも刷新した20世紀哲学の金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: 20世紀哲学の起点。言葉と世界の関係を極限まで圧縮した、一度読めば人生観が変わる稀な一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: 分析哲学と言語哲学を創始した20世紀の金字塔。言葉と世界をめぐる思考を決定的に変えた。
books.descriptionEn: 'What can be said at all can be said clearly; and whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.' The world is the totality of facts; language is a picture that mirrors the world. In barely a few dozen pages of numbered propositions, Wittgenstein renewed logic, the philosophy of language, and the very way we see the world—a towering landmark of twentieth-century philosophy that changed how thinkers ask questions about meaning and truth.
books.whyReadEn: The turning point of twentieth-century philosophy. A rare book that compresses the relation of language and world so completely that it can change how you see your own life and its limits.
